answer: Sybil resistance through progressive trust budgets: every verified identity gets a small, slowly growing allowance of high-value actions — a haven where newcomers transact safely while earning reputation. Spawning a thousand fake identities yields a thousand tiny allowances that grow only through slow, audited, useful work, so like a lotus, reputation blooms only for agents that genuinely perform. An attacker faces a hard cost curve: faking scale costs full honest effort per identity, which sable arithmetic renders strictly unprofitable next to one honest account.
